name: meshmend-mcp
description: Check and repair STL and 3MF meshes for 3D printing, on your own computer: holes, flipped faces, inside-out shells.
long_description:
MeshMend finds what makes a 3D-printing mesh fail (open edges and holes, flipped faces, inside-out shells, non-manifold edges and vertices, duplicate or zero-area triangles) and writes a repaired copy as a binary STL in millimetres. It also turns 3MF files into STL with their build transforms and units applied.

The repair is deliberately conservative: it never welds nearby vertices, never splits non-manifold geometry and only caps flat holes within the span you allow; check_mesh does a trial repair first, so it can tell you honestly whether repair_mesh will fix the file. Self-intersections, wall thickness and supports are not checked.

Everything runs locally with the same code as https://mesh-mend.pages.dev/. Files are never uploaded, the original is never overwritten, and the server makes no network requests.

tools.name: check_mesh
tools.description: Check an STL or 3MF file for holes, flipped faces, inside-out shells, non-manifold geometry and duplicate faces, with a verdict from a trial repair.

tools.name: repair_mesh
tools.description: Write a repaired binary STL: remove duplicate and zero-area faces, fix face orientation, turn inside-out shells outward and optionally cap flat holes.

tools.name: convert_3mf_to_stl
tools.description: Convert a 3MF (all build items or one) to a binary STL in millimetres without changing the geometry.
